chapter: Ellington colleagues, singers and world tours
title: Later singers: Tony Watkins, Jimmy McPhail, Lil Greenwood, Ray Nance
summary: He recalls these singers, who came and went, noting only Ivie stayed.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them

blocks.x: Tony Watkins?

Tony came in with the spiritual or the concerts -- spiritual concerts -- and he did very well. He fitted -- fit that format very well, but for some reason they come and they go. I guess -- if it isn't money, it's to a better and more advantageous position, but they go.

And Tony's first appearance with the band was at San Francisco in Grace Cathedral, at the first sacred concert in 1965. (Unintelligible) He was 16 years old, and he came in to and sang The Lord's Prayer and then left. Eventually he joined the (Unintelligible) band and sang part of the time and was band boy part of the time.
And valet and everything.
(Laughter)
Well, it's--
(Unintelligible) -- Jimmy -- Jimmy oh -- were you there when he --
Grissom Goodman
No, I didn't know Jimmy.
Don Grissom -- Ben Goodman's nephew.
I know.
I knew that much, but I mean to work with him, I didn't know him.
And Jimmy McPhail?

Jimmy McPhail -- Jimmy McPhail worked also with the band. First time I saw him, he came to Vegas or what's that other town out of Vegas -- Tahoe -- and worked, and then he was with the band for quite a while. He has a bar in Washington, doing quite well.
Yeah, he worked for (unintelligible) -- in 'My Peo
Yes.
-- and (unintelligible). And Lily on several Sacred Concerts Greenwood?

Lily was out of -- I think they picked her up in San Francisco. She was singing in that -- it was that place downstairs, was kind of cellar place up in San Francisco. She did quite well too for a while. As I say, they come and they go. They don't -- the only one that stayed was Ivy. She stayed forever. But most of the rest of them come and go.
What do you think of Ray Nance's singing?
Perfect for what he did, the little jovial youngster type of work, and nothing serious. He wasn't a serious singer. He was the jovial type of singer.
